title: Ozempic Linked to Fewer Bone Fractures
hook: Losing weight often costs you bone. Yet a study of nearly 60,000 people with type 2 diabetes found semaglutide users had about 15% fewer fractures — even though they lost more weight.
key_points: A real-world study analyzed health records from nearly 60,000 adults with type 2 diabetes.
Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus) users had about 15% fewer bone fractures.
That's notable because they lost more weight than people on other weight-loss drugs.
Weight loss can otherwise come at the expense of bone, making the protection a surprise.
content_html: Rapid weight loss has a known downside: it can weaken bone along with fat, leaving people more prone to fractures. So a large real-world study turned up an unexpected bonus for people with type 2 diabetes taking semaglutide — sold as Ozempic, Wegovy, and Rybelsus — who came out ahead on bones, not behind.
extra_html:
Analyzing health records from nearly 60,000 adults, ScienceDaily reports, researchers found semaglutide users had about 15% fewer bone fractures than people taking other common weight-loss medications — and that was despite losing more weight, not less.

The finding is an association from health records, not proof that the drug strengthens bone, and it speaks to people with type 2 diabetes specifically. But it adds to a growing list of effects these medications seem to have beyond blood sugar and the scale, and it's a reassuring signal for a worry that often comes with significant weight loss.

related.title: Protecting Your Bones
related.hook: Bone looks permanent, but it's living tissue that thins with age. Osteoporosis weakens it silently until a minor fall causes a major break.

related.title: Why GLP-1 Drugs Don't Work for Everyone
related.hook: Scientists found genetic variants — carried by roughly 1 in 10 people — that seem to cause a kind of 'GLP-1 resistance,' making drugs like Ozempic less effective at controlling blood sugar.
